text:
maria: heads up — sudden p99 jump in hosted us-east-1 at 11:02 UTC, p99 ~1.8s from baseline ~220ms. started 11:02:00, lasted ~2m. seeing queue growth on runtime-pool-7 :eyes:

dylan: yep, alerted by alertbot. p95 also climbed but less dramatic. traces show a kernel_selector switch around 11:02:00 on pool-7.

arjun: any deployments at that time?

deploy-bot: deploy to runtime-pool-7 started by ci/canary at 11:01:58 (commit abc123).

kim: KV cache miss rate spiked on pool-7 at 11:02:01 — miss_rate 3% -> 36% in metrics. priming churn looks likely.

maria: that aligns with the kernel switch. when kselector falls back to aux kernels we see slower per-token times for short sequences.

nate: tenant svc-finance-3 had a burst of tiny requests (avg tokens 12) — ~30k reqs/min, probably hotshard. rate limiter didn't kick early because requests were under per-request cost threshold.

dylan: batch sampler stats: micro-batch ratio jumped (batches of size 1-3) at the same time, so batching overhead + wrong kernel = p99 multiplier.

arjun: can you paste the sampler snapshot and the simple log of kernel decisions?

kim: here's the relevant snippet from metrics/logs:
```
11:01:57 sampler.window=128 target_batch=16
11:01:58 kselector: preferred->optimized (commit abc123)
11:02:00 sampler.micro_batch_rate=0.72
11:02:01 kselector: fallback->aux_kernel_v2 (latency_penalty_detected)
11:02:02 kvcache.miss_rate(pool-7)=0.36
11:02:03 batch.size.p50=2 batch.size.p95=6
```

maria: thanks. so chain: deploy changed kernel selection heuristic -> priming or kernel mismatch -> kvcache churn + microbatches -> p99 spike.

dylan: looks like kselector's priming threshold was lowered in commit abc123. for short sequences that hurts.

nate: proposed immediate mitigations: 1) roll back kselector change on pool-7, 2) add a soft throttle on svc-finance-3, 3) bump sampler aggregation window for pool-7 to 256 for 5m.

arjun: agree. roll back first, then sampler bump, then throttle if still noisy. who will run the rollback?

maria: i'll kick the rollback for pool-7 now. marking as high-priority.

maria: /run rollback-runtime --pool=pool-7 --to=abc122 (previous)

deploy-bot: rollback initiated for runtime-pool-7 by maria at 11:04:10. estimated time ~45s.

kim: after rollback, kvcache miss rate trending back down (11:04:55 miss_rate -> 4%). batch sizes recovering to p50=12 p95=30.

dylan: p99 back to ~230ms at 11:05:10. nice.

nate: still seeing a small burst from svc-finance-3, but rate is within limits; we throttled temporarily at the edge (edge-throttle applied to tenant id).

maria: follow-ups: arjun to file a perf regression PR for the kselector change, add a test that simulates short-seq bursts in CI. kim to add a dashboard compare for kselector priming thresholds. dylan to propose sampler default for hosted pools. nate to review tenant throttling policy. I'll open the incident ticket.

arjun: filing PR and linking this thread.

alertbot: incident opened: INC-2026-1843, sev2, owners: maria/arjun/kim.

maria: thanks everyone. summary: kernel-selection change in abc123 caused regression for short-seq micro-batch workloads, amplified by a noisy tenant and KV cache priming churn. rollback fixed p99. next: regression test + safer rollout gating for kselector heuristics. :white_check_mark:
